finding: Pharmaceutical thromboembolic prophylaxis 45%; early mobilisation 56%.
change: Results of the 1992 audit and indicator standards circulated to orthopaedic and care of the elderly consultants and audit leads at each hospital.
setting: Seven hospitals with trauma orthopaedic departments, East Anglia (multi-site audit)
cycle1_result: Pharmaceutical thromboembolic prophylaxis 45%; early mobilisation 56%.
intervention: Results of the 1992 audit and indicator standards circulated to orthopaedic and care of the elderly consultants and audit leads at each hospital.
cycle2_result: Pharmaceutical thromboembolic prophylaxis 81%; early mobilisation 70%; reduced pneumonia, wound infection, pressure sores and fatal PE.
other_findings: No change in 3-month functional outcome or mortality; some hospitals failed to maintain good practice.

topic: Blood transfusion and cross-matching in arthroplasty
title: Audit on the efficient use of cross-matched blood in elective total hip and total knee replacement.
standard: Maximum Surgical Blood Ordering Schedule (MSBOS) and national guidelines
finding: High level of unnecessary cross-matched blood; THR cross-match transfusion (C:T) ratio 3.21

topic: Blood transfusion and cross-matching in arthroplasty

finding: 11% of patients undergoing primary TKA required post-operative transfusion.

cycle1_result: 11% of patients undergoing primary TKA required post-operative transfusion.

cycle2_result: 17 of 233 patients (7%) received allogeneic blood, average two units; no statistically significant difference from the first audit.

title: Using clinical audit to improve the quality of obstetric care at the Tibetan Delek Hospital in North India: a longitudinal study.

change: Multidisciplinary Rapid Recovery Group with parallel PDSA cycles: ropivacaine local infiltration protocol, oxycodone MR, preprinted drug charts, Taurus frames and nurse-led mobilisation, stopping routine MSU and TED stockings, and a ring-fenced elective ward.
setting: North Devon District Hospital, elective hip and knee replacement pathway
cycle1_result: Mean length of stay 3.6 days for both total hip and total knee replacement; Model Hospital median length of stay 4.2 days (hips, 41st nationally) and 3.9 days (knees, 34th).
intervention: Multidisciplinary Rapid Recovery Group with parallel PDSA cycles: ropivacaine local infiltration protocol, oxycodone MR, preprinted drug charts, Taurus frames and nurse-led mobilisation, stopping routine MSU and TED stockings, and a ring-fenced elective ward.

title: Crossing quartiles: Improving time to theatre for patients with hip fractures in a large UK district general hospital; A quality improvement report.
standard: Hip fracture Best Practice Tariff: surgery within 36 hours of admission (National Hip Fracture Database)
finding: Surgery within 36 hours 54%; mean time to surgery 43.68 hours; BPT achieved in 45.7%; trust ranked 152/160 for time to surgery.
change: Anaesthetic 'hot week' introduced in January 2018: the same anaesthetist covers hip fracture lists, attends trauma meeting, liaises with orthopaedic and orthogeriatric teams and advises on medical optimisation.
setting: Pinderfields General Hospital, Mid Yorkshire Hospitals NHS Trust (large district general hospital)
cycle1_result: Surgery within 36 hours 54%; mean time to surgery 43.68 hours; BPT achieved in 45.7%; trust ranked 152/160 for time to surgery.
intervention: Anaesthetic 'hot week' introduced in January 2018: the same anaesthetist covers hip fracture lists, attends trauma meeting, liaises with orthopaedic and orthogeriatric teams and advises on medical optimisation.
cycle2_result: Surgery within 36 hours 87.5%; mean time to surgery 25.11 hours; BPT achieved in 84%; ranking rose to 20th for time to surgery and 18th for BPT.
other_findings: Rescheduled operations fell from 126 to 31 and mean length of stay fell by 5.1 days; mortality unchanged. The unit sees on average 551 hip fractures a year. Abstract only.
authors: Anthony C; Malaj M; Lokanathan P; Murgatroyd J; O'Connor P

title: Clinical Audit as a Quality Improvement Tool in Measurements of Lying and Standing Blood Pressure for Elderly Patients Admitted With a Hip Fracture.

cycle1_result: LSBP measured in 16 (32%); correctly documented in 12/16 (75%).
intervention: Results presented at geriatric medicine mortality meeting with root cause analysis; flyers and posters on wards, teaching sessions for ward staff on LSBP measurement and recording on POET, and aide-memoires placed around wards.

topic: Fracture clinic standards and virtual fracture clinic
title: Optimizing orthopedic trauma care delivery during the COVID-19 pandemic. A closed-loop audit of implementing a virtual fracture clinic and fast-track pathway in a Dutch level 2 trauma center.
standard: Predefined standards from national coronavirus outpatient guidelines and local consensus: (1) all eligible ED trauma patients referred for VFC review; (2) all patients contacted after VFC review; (3) patient-initiated follow-up by default where possible; (4) follow-up by telephone or video where possible. Target 100% for standard 1.
finding: 162/184 (88.0%) referred for VFC review; 98.1% reached afterwards (3 patients, 1.9%, not reached); 29/162 (17.9%) discharged 'virtually'; 137/291 (45.0%) appointments remote. Median total ED time 95 minutes vs 131 minutes at baseline (p<0.001).
change: After an evaluation meeting, ED staff were invited to attend VFC review for direct feedback, presentations explaining the workflow were held, posters were put up in the ED, and a patient information leaflet asking patients to call if not contacted by 15:00 the next workday was introduced.
setting: OLVG, a level 2 trauma centre and teaching hospital in Amsterdam (emergency department and virtual fracture clinic)
cycle1_result: 162/184 (88.0%) referred for VFC review; 98.1% reached afterwards (3 patients, 1.9%, not reached); 29/162 (17.9%) discharged 'virtually'; 137/291 (45.0%) appointments remote. Median total ED time 95 minutes vs 131 minutes at baseline (p<0.001).
intervention: After an evaluation meeting, ED staff were invited to attend VFC review for direct feedback, presentations explaining the workflow were held, posters were put up in the ED, and a patient information leaflet asking patients to call if not contacted by 15:00 the next workday was introduced.
cycle2_result: 302/305 (98.4%) referred for VFC review; 99.0% reached afterwards (3 patients, 1.0%, not reached); 41/302 (13.6%) discharged 'virtually'; 179/436 (41.1%) appointments remote. Median total ED time 98 minutes (−33 minutes vs baseline, p=0.001); time to review 47 minutes (p<0.001); time for review 35 minutes vs 45 minutes (p=0.019).
other_findings: An ED orthopaedic trauma fast-track pathway was introduced alongside the VFC; 88% and 92% of suspected fracture patients were treated in fast-track rooms. Median VFC review time was 9 minutes then 7 minutes per patient.
authors: Geerdink TH; Salentijn DA; de Vries KA; Noordman PCW; van Dongen JM; Haverlag R; Goslings JC; van Veen RN
citation: Geerdink TH, Salentijn DA, de Vries KA, Noordman PCW, van Dongen JM, Haverlag R, et al.. Optimizing orthopedic trauma care delivery during the COVID-19 pandemic. A closed-loop audit of implementing a virtual fracture clinic and fast-track pathway in a Dutch level 2 trauma center. Trauma Surg Acute Care Open. 2021;6(1):e000691. doi:10.1136/tsaco-2021-000691. PMID: 34632079.

topic: Hip fracture analgesia and nerve block

change: Results discussed at departmental and Trust mortality meetings, one-to-one teaching on loss-of-resistance FICB for ED and T&O junior doctors, and enforcing completion of the hip fracture clinical proforma with FICB sign-off or documented contraindication

cycle1_result: FICB administered in 45 (24.5%); mean post-FICB pain score 4 (NRS)

title: Introduction of an enhanced recovery programme for total shoulder arthroplasty: report of a novel pathway.
standard: not reported
finding: Pre-enhanced recovery: mean LOS 2.38 nights, median 2 nights, single night stay rate 40.2%; complication rate 9.9%.
change: Enhanced recovery programme via PDSA cycles: MDT-led preoperative class with OT home assessment, new patient information booklet and DVD, standardised anaesthetic/analgesic protocol with carbohydrate and gabapentin loading, and a physiotherapy protocol with sling for comfort only and early safe-zone mobilisation.
setting: Derby Shoulder Unit, University Hospitals of Derby and Burton NHS Foundation Trust
cycle1_result: Pre-enhanced recovery: mean LOS 2.38 nights, median 2 nights, single night stay rate 40.2%; complication rate 9.9%.
intervention: Enhanced recovery programme via PDSA cycles: MDT-led preoperative class with OT home assessment, new patient information booklet and DVD, standardised anaesthetic/analgesic protocol with carbohydrate and gabapentin loading, and a physiotherapy protocol with sling for comfort only and early safe-zone mobilisation.
cycle2_period: 6 October 2017 pilot; full roll-out 7 December 2017 to 8 October 2018
cycle2_result: Matched enhanced recovery cohort: mean LOS 1.89 nights (median 2), single night stay rate 49.2%; 15 fewer bed nights; complication rate 7%; OSS and Constant scores similar at 3 and 12 months.
other_findings: Adherence to dexamethasone use was only 36% (80% on re-audit of 15 patients) and gabapentin compliance only 24%; 12 patients had discharge delays because social services would not accept pre-admission referral.
authors: Morgan ML; Davies-Jones GR; Ibrahim EF; Booker SJ; Bateman M; Tambe AA; Clark DI
citation: Morgan ML, Davies-Jones GR, Ibrahim EF, Booker SJ, Bateman M, Tambe AA, et al.. Introduction of an enhanced recovery programme for total shoulder arthroplasty: report of a novel pathway. BMJ Open Qual. 2021;10(4):e001371. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2021-001371. PMID: 34670774.

finding: Abbreviations in 189/350 (54%) forms; mostly by registrars (74%); DVT and PE commonest.

cycle1_result: Abbreviations in 189/350 (54%) forms; mostly by registrars (74%); DVT and PE commonest.
intervention: Results presented at M&M meeting, email to all staff, reminder sticker attached to consent forms and poster in areas where consent is taken.
other_findings: DVT and PE remained the commonest abbreviations; use of CRPS, PIP and EUA rose in proportion.

topic: Bone protection and secondary fracture prevention
title: Improving Secondary Bone Protection Prescription in Patients Admitted With a Femoral Neck Fracture.
standard: Royal College of Physicians National Hip Fracture Database: all patients with hip fracture assessed for and managed with a secondary bone-protection plan (100% gold standard); SMART aim of an additional 40% per year
finding: 13.9% (n=11) assessed for bone protection; 1.3% (n=1) prescribed a bisphosphonate and 10.1% (n=8) other bone protection; 86.1% (n=68) neither assessed nor prescribed.
change: PDSA 1 awareness poster (January 2019); PDSA 2 education session for clerking and ward doctors added to induction (March 2019); PDSA 3 MDT meeting with responsibility charting, giving assessment and prescribing to the care of the elderly team (April 2019).
setting: Orthopaedic wards of a large district general hospital with a level 2 trauma centre
cycle1_result: 13.9% (n=11) assessed for bone protection; 1.3% (n=1) prescribed a bisphosphonate and 10.1% (n=8) other bone protection; 86.1% (n=68) neither assessed nor prescribed.
intervention: PDSA 1 awareness poster (January 2019); PDSA 2 education session for clerking and ward doctors added to induction (March 2019); PDSA 3 MDT meeting with responsibility charting, giving assessment and prescribing to the care of the elderly team (April 2019).
cycle2_period: April 2019 (a fortnight after the MDT meeting)
cycle2_result: 100% (n=50) of patients assessed or placed on a bone-protection plan.
other_findings: PDSA 1 (n=27) 44.4% (p<0.01) and PDSA 2 (n=21) 76% (p<0.001); an annual re-audit of 50 patients during the COVID-19 pandemic showed 100% was sustained. At baseline 89.9% of patients and relatives were unaware of bone protection.
authors: Hamid M; Chikhlia A; Gogna A

title: Improving the Quality of Medical Documentation in Orthopedic Surgical Notes Using the Surgical Tool for Auditing Records (STAR) Score.
standard: Surgical Tool for Auditing Records (STAR), based on Royal College of Surgeons guidance on medical record keeping (no target stated)
finding: Mean total STAR score 94.3 ± 1.6.
change: Annual teaching of practitioners on documentation using slides based on Royal College of Surgeons of England recommendations, with periodic (annual) re-auditing.
setting: Jordan University Hospital, Amman, tertiary academic hospital; elective orthopaedic surgery records
cycle1_result: Mean total STAR score 94.3 ± 1.6.
intervention: Annual teaching of practitioners on documentation using slides based on Royal College of Surgeons of England recommendations, with periodic (annual) re-auditing.
other_findings: Yearly audits 2016–2021 (454 records) showed scores of 95.5, 95.9, 95.7 and 96.8 for 2017–2020; consent and anaesthetic domains plateaued. Benefits on the consent form and post-op instructions were never documented, and suture details fell to 41.5%.

title: Results From an All Wales Trainee Led Collaborative Prospective Audit on Management of Ankle Fractures.
standard: BOAST guideline on management of ankle fractures (documentation, imaging including CT for posterior malleolus, weight-bearing X-rays, early weight-bearing)
finding: Documentation: mechanism 94.4%, skin 71.3%, neurovascular status 80.1%, comorbidities 81%, alcohol 34.3%, smoking 41.7%. Mortice view 75.9%. Early weight-bearing 63/106 (59.43%) non-operative and 11/110 (10%) operative.

cycle1_result: Documentation: mechanism 94.4%, skin 71.3%, neurovascular status 80.1%, comorbidities 81%, alcohol 34.3%, smoking 41.7%. Mortice view 75.9%. intervention: not reported

title: Informed Written Consent for Orthopaedic Trauma in the Emergency Setting at a Tertiary Referral Centre: A Closed-Loop Audit.
standard: American Association of Orthopaedic Surgeons 'Orthopaedic Surgical Consent' standards (name, DOB, board number, procedure without abbreviation, side/site stated); no target stated
finding: Name, DOB and board number 100%. No abbreviations 79 (74.5%). Side/site 81 (76.4%) (the abstract wording says 'without correctly stating' but the comparison treats this as compliance). Abbreviation and side/site both failing in 13 (12.3%).

setting: Galway University Hospitals, tertiary referral centre; consent forms for emergency orthopaedic trauma surgery
cycle1_result: Name, DOB and board number 100%. No abbreviations 79 (74.5%). Side/site 81 (76.4%) (the abstract wording says 'without correctly stating' but the comparison treats this as compliance). Abbreviation and side/site both failing in 13 (12.3%).
intervention: A single 90-minute virtual education session for all trauma and orthopaedic staff on consent standards, sharing cycle 1 results.
cycle2_result: Name, DOB and board number 100%. No abbreviations 37 (92.5%, p=0.02). Side/site correctly stated 39 (97.5%, p=0.0015). No form had both failures (0% vs 12.3%, p=0.02).

finding: Documented attempt to contact NoK 80% (24/30); NoK section of Consent Form Four completed 30% (10/30).

title: A retrospective analysis of the definitive management of open talus fractures at a major trauma centre, comparing ORIF to FUSION: cohort study and audit of BOAST 4 guidelines.
standard: BOAST 4 guidelines for open fractures (e.g. prophylactic antibiotics within one hour of injury, definitive soft tissue coverage within 72 h, orthoplastic involvement, debridement); no target stated
finding: 15 open talus fractures in 14 patients. 100% had orthoplastic involvement, initial saline-soaked gauze and occlusive film dressing, functional recovery and rehabilitation advice, and recorded debridement; 60% had debridement using fasciotomy lines. Only 27% received prophylactic antibiotics within one hour of injury and only 27% achieved definitive soft tissue coverage within 72 h (mean 9.7 days in the 7 needing coverage).
setting: Addenbrooke's Major Trauma Unit, Cambridge University Hospitals; major trauma centre, open talus fractures in skeletally mature patients
cycle1_result: 15 open talus fractures in 14 patients. 100% had orthoplastic involvement, initial saline-soaked gauze and occlusive film dressing, functional recovery and rehabilitation advice, and recorded debridement; 60% had debridement using fasciotomy lines. intervention: not reported
other_findings: Mainly a cohort comparison: no significant difference between ORIF and tibiocalcaneal fusion in EQ-5D-5L (p = 0.13), FAAM-ADL (p = 0.20), FAAM-Sport (p = 0.34) or infection rate (p = 0.55); deep infection occurred in 7 cases (47%).

topic: Suspected cauda equina time to MRI
title: Compliance With the Cauda Equina Pathway: Results of a Closed-Loop Audit.
standard: Local standard operating procedure for acute back pain with suspected cauda equina syndrome, based on BASS/SBNS guidance (senior ED discussion, anal tone and perianal sensation documented, MRI within 24 hours, spinal centre plan documented); no target stated
finding: ED assessment and senior discussion 24 (96%); discussion with spinal centre by senior ED doctor 13 (61.9%); anal tone documented 23 (92%); perianal sensation documented 18 (72%); spinal centre plan documented per SOP 5 (20%); MRI within 24 hours 25 (100%).
change: Teaching on CES and neurological examination for T&O and ED juniors, posters of the pathway in ED, discussion between T&O and ED on GP referrals, and emails to staff; an electronic SBAR documentation template was also created.
setting: Non-specialist admitting district hospital (Warrington and Halton Teaching Hospital, per affiliation); emergency department and trauma and orthopaedics, referring to a tertiary spinal centre
cycle1_result: ED assessment and senior discussion 24 (96%); discussion with spinal centre by senior ED doctor 13 (61.9%); anal tone documented 23 (92%); perianal sensation documented 18 (72%); spinal centre plan documented per SOP 5 (20%); MRI within 24 hours 25 (100%).
intervention: Teaching on CES and neurological examination for T&O and ED juniors, posters of the pathway in ED, discussion between T&O and ED on GP referrals, and emails to staff; an electronic SBAR documentation template was also created.
cycle2_result: ED assessment and senior discussion 26 (90%, p=0.727); discussion by senior ED doctor 2 (9%, p=0.000); anal tone documented 28 (97%, p=0.887); perianal sensation documented 28 (97%, p=0.028); spinal centre plan documented 0 (0%, p=0.033); MRI within 24 hours 29 (100%).

title: Preventing pressure ulcers from paediatric femoral traction: use of an audit cycle to assess a new concise manual and a daily care chart.
standard: not reported
finding: Three patients (23%) developed grade 2 pressure sores; mean traction 8.5 days; pressure site check documented in only 7.7%.
change: New single-page traction manual and daily care chart introduced into patient care notes.
setting: Birmingham Women's and Children's NHS Foundation Trust; children with femoral shaft fracture in skin traction
cycle1_result: Three patients (23%) developed grade 2 pressure sores; mean traction 8.5 days; pressure site check documented in only 7.7%.

title: Can introducing a direct endocrine pathway reduce hyponatraemia in elective knee and hip replacements? A closed-loop audit and service evaluation study.
standard: Hyponatraemia protocol based on NICE guidance (sodium cut-off 133 mmol/l per local guidance); no numeric target stated
finding: Hyponatraemia in 36 (12%); only 38% of hyponatraemic patients investigated, 33% had endocrine input; mean 3.6 days to endocrine referral; length of stay 7.7 vs 4.6 days; 4 of 11 profound cases admitted to critical care (8 days in total).
change: Direct endocrine pathway developed with endocrinology based on NICE guidance: protocol poster displayed in clinical areas and agreement for same-day endocrine review of arthroplasty patients referred via ICE.
setting: Elective arthroplasty unit, Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
cycle1_result: Hyponatraemia in 36 (12%); only 38% of hyponatraemic patients investigated, 33% had endocrine input; mean 3.6 days to endocrine referral; length of stay 7.7 vs 4.6 days; 4 of 11 profound cases admitted to critical care (8 days in total).
intervention: Direct endocrine pathway developed with endocrinology based on NICE guidance: protocol poster displayed in clinical areas and agreement for same-day endocrine review of arthroplasty patients referred via ICE.
cycle2_result: Hyponatraemia in 31 (11.7%); all 3 profound cases investigated and referred to endocrinology; mean 2.3 days to endocrine referral; length of stay reduced by 0.7 days (p = 0.008144); no critical care admissions (p = 0.031622).
other_findings: Hyponatraemia was more common after knee than hip replacement and in older patients in both cycles; symptoms and fluids were not assessed in cycle 2.
authors: Waller M; Barkley S; Harrison T
journal: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England
citation: Waller M, Barkley S, Harrison T. Can introducing a direct endocrine pathway reduce hyponatraemia in elective knee and hip replacements? A closed-loop audit and service evaluation study. Ann R Coll Surg Engl. 2025;107(7):469-472. doi:10.1308/rcsann.2021.0296. PMID: 35175142.

finding: 16/41 (39%) received their medications correctly; 22 critical drug class omissions; 19 omitted because nil by mouth.

cycle1_result: 16/41 (39%) received their medications correctly; 22 critical drug class omissions; 19 omitted because nil by mouth.
intervention: Poster on drug trolleys listing which medications to give or withhold, meetings with ward managers and nursing staff, and presentation at orthopaedic and anaesthetic audit meetings.

title: Early Management of Paediatric Wrist and Forearm Fractures in a Busy District General Hospital Emergency Department: A Retrospective Cohort Comparison Study and Audit of BOAST Guidelines.
standard: BOAST early management of distal forearm fractures in children (May 2021): early ED manipulation, neurovascular and consent documentation, orthogonal X-rays, fracture clinic within 7 days
finding: 23/72 (31.94%) manipulated in ED; 11 of 23 ED manipulations failed.
change: Local trust pathway in line with BOAST introduced from July 2021 (analgesia/sedation, location, manipulation and referral guidance) with staff education.
setting: Emergency department, district general hospital with paediatric orthopaedic services, Gloucestershire Royal Hospital
cycle1_result: 23/72 (31.94%) manipulated in ED; 11 of 23 ED manipulations failed.
intervention: Local trust pathway in line with BOAST introduced from July 2021 (analgesia/sedation, location, manipulation and referral guidance) with staff education.
cycle2_result: 73/87 manipulated in ED (p<0.00001); 63 (86.31%) acceptable reduction, 10 (13.69%) failed. cycle1_result: 33/84 discharged at first visit; 69 had a single X-ray, 12 had two and 4 had three X-rays

title: Orthopaedic Out of Bed Project (OOBP): improving early mobilisation following femoral fracture using a therapy-led education programme.
standard: NHFD metric: patient mobilised (standing or hoisted) out of bed by the day after surgery; target at least the UK national average of 81%
finding: Mean 60% of patients mobilised by the day after surgery. Hip Sprint cohort (n=60): 1.7% mobilised by healthcare assistants before physiotherapy assessment.
change: Therapy-led ward education programme for trauma healthcare assistants (1-hour 2:1 face-to-face session plus observed sign-off), ward posters and Trust media campaign, delivered over two PDSA cycles (June-July 2020 and June-August 2022)
setting: 35-bed trauma ward, James Paget University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (district general hospital), Great Yarmouth
cycle1_period: 6 months before the intervention (2019/2020, NHFD data); Hip Sprint audit September and December 2019
cycle1_result: Mean 60% of patients mobilised by the day after surgery. Hip Sprint cohort (n=60): 1.7% mobilised by healthcare assistants before physiotherapy assessment.
intervention: Therapy-led ward education programme for trauma healthcare assistants (1-hour 2:1 face-to-face session plus observed sign-off), ward posters and Trust media campaign, delivered over two PDSA cycles (June-July 2020 and June-August 2022)
cycle2_result: Mean 79.2% mobilised by the day after surgery after PDSA cycle 2 (from 60% in 2019). Healthcare assistant mobilisation before physiotherapy assessment 30% (n=51 cohort).
other_findings: After PDSA cycle 1 the rate rose to a mean of 78% but fell back to 71.8% in 2021, attributed to staff turnover. 30-day mortality fell from 10.1% to 7% between 2019 and 2022 (causality not established).
authors: Gray R; Taylor M; Bullock R

title: An Audit on the Pre-operative Fasting Time of Trauma-List Orthopaedic Patients at a District General Hospital in Chichester, United Kingdom.
standard: RCN, AAGBI, European Society of Anaesthesiology and ASA guidelines: fasting of two hours for clear fluids and six hours for solids
finding: All 50 patients (100%) fasted beyond six hours for solids (mean 15.8 hours, range 9–24) and 49 (98%) beyond two hours for clear fluids (mean 10.5 hours, range 2–20); only 5 (10%) had correct documented fasting instructions; 31 (62%) were 'nil by mouth from midnight'.
setting: Orthopaedic trauma list, St Richard's Hospital, district general hospital, Chichester
cycle1_result: All 50 patients (100%) fasted beyond six hours for solids (mean 15.8 hours, range 9–24) and 49 (98%) beyond two hours for clear fluids (mean 10.5 hours, range 2–20); only 5 (10%) had correct documented fasting instructions; 31 (62%) were 'nil by mouth from midnight'.
intervention: not reported
other_findings: Staff survey showed poor knowledge: only 42.9% of ward nurses knew the 6 hour/2 hour rule. Only 52% received preoperative IV fluids; a 'sip till send' policy has since been introduced.

title: Development of a New Knee Arthroscopy Operative Proforma Saving Thousands of British Pounds.
standard: Correct ICD-10 and OPCS-4 coding of arthroscopic knee procedures from the operation note; proforma based on Royal College guidance for operation notes
finding: 17/34 (50%) cases coded incorrectly; tariff value £85,026 as coded versus £114,351 after correction, a loss of £29,325.
change: New coding-friendly knee arthroscopy operation note proforma with tick boxes, developed with coding staff and agreed at a consensus meeting, disseminated by email, notice boards and governance meetings.
setting: Two centres of one trauma and orthopaedic service (Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust / North Manchester General Hospital), knee arthroscopy day cases
cycle1_result: 17/34 (50%) cases coded incorrectly; tariff value £85,026 as coded versus £114,351 after correction, a loss of £29,325.
intervention: New coding-friendly knee arthroscopy operation note proforma with tick boxes, developed with coding staff and agreed at a consensus meeting, disseminated by email, notice boards and governance meetings.
cycle2_result: 2/37 (5%) cases coded incorrectly; £86,886 as coded versus £89,540 after correction, a loss of £2654.
other_findings: Most coding errors came from vague documentation of preoperative diagnoses and additional procedures (e.g. extra meniscectomy or cartilage debridement). Uptake of the proforma was slow and some cases were excluded for incorrect use of the form.

cycle1_result: Mechanism of injury 86%; skin integrity 54%; circulation status 54%; detailed vascular examination 17%; neurological examination 54%; sensory detail 48%; MRC motor scale 48%; repeat neurovascular examination after reduction 56%; overall precise documentation of clinical findings 17%.

topic: Suspected cauda equina time to MRI

cycle1_result: Mean MRI waiting time 12.5 hours (8am-4pm 9.5 h; 4pm-12am 18 h; 12am-8am 8.5 h); same-day discharge 27 (29%); inpatient stay 66 (71%)
intervention: Introduction of a middle-grade trauma and orthopaedic doctor in the emergency department (urgent treatment centre) to assess suspected CES patients

title: Improving Completion Rates of Treatment Escalation Plan (TEP) in a London Teaching Hospital: A Quality Improvement Study.
standard: Trust treatment escalation plan (TEP) policy: TEP completed for emergency adult admissions, within 48 hours
finding: Overall TEP completion 69.5%; completed within 48 hours 47.82%; mean time to complete 4.4 days; mean overrides 3.2; longest 35 days; 24 instances of skipping. Incomplete TEPs 30.4% (n=7).
change: Revised local TEP pathway/algorithm allowing F1+ doctors to complete TEPs for young patients with simple fractures, algorithm displayed in trauma room, emails, individual teaching, and reminders to discuss TEP status on the post-take ward round.
setting: Orthopaedic wards, University Hospital Lewisham (London teaching hospital), adult inpatients
cycle1_result: Overall TEP completion 69.5%; completed within 48 hours 47.82%; mean time to complete 4.4 days; mean overrides 3.2; longest 35 days; 24 instances of skipping. Incomplete TEPs 30.4% (n=7).
intervention: Revised local TEP pathway/algorithm allowing F1+ doctors to complete TEPs for young patients with simple fractures, algorithm displayed in trauma room, emails, individual teaching, and reminders to discuss TEP status on the post-take ward round.

topic: Elective cancellations due to asymptomatic bacteriuria
title: Introduction of a New Protocol to Limit the Number of Cancelled Elective Orthopaedic Operations Due to Asymptomatic Bacteriuria.
standard: not reported
finding: Of 33 all-cause cancellations, 7 (21.2%) were cancelled for UTI risk on positive urinalysis; only 1 (14.3%) of these was symptomatic, so 6 (85.7%) were cancelled for asymptomatic bacteriuria.
change: New symptom-based protocol from 1 May 2019: all patients complete a 7-item UTI symptom questionnaire and surgery is cancelled only if two or more symptoms are reported, regardless of urinalysis.
setting: Lister Hospital, Stevenage (East & North Herts NHS Trust), large district general hospital offering tertiary orthopaedic services; cancelled elective orthopaedic operations
cycle1_result: Of 33 all-cause cancellations, 7 (21.2%) were cancelled for UTI risk on positive urinalysis; only 1 (14.3%) of these was symptomatic, so 6 (85.7%) were cancelled for asymptomatic bacteriuria.
intervention: New symptom-based protocol from 1 May 2019: all patients complete a 7-item UTI symptom questionnaire and surgery is cancelled only if two or more symptoms are reported, regardless of urinalysis.
cycle2_result: Of 45 all-cause cancellations, 2 (4.4%) were cancelled for UTI risk, both symptomatic; 4 (8.8%) had positive urinalysis, the 2 asymptomatic ones cancelled for unrelated reasons. No cancellations for asymptomatic bacteriuria; estimated 71.4% reduction in cancellations for UTI risk.

title: Understanding Barriers to Early Rehabilitation Following the Surgery for Fragility Hip Fractures: A Single-Centre Audit.
standard: National guidelines (NICE): mobilisation on the day of or the day after hip fracture surgery; two hours of physiotherapy in the first week after surgery; no target stated
finding: 93% (106/113) seen by a physiotherapist on the day of or day after surgery (main orthopaedic ward 94%, 80/85; outliers 93%, 21/28; P=0.3). 40% (46/113) had delayed mobilisation. 83% (94/113) had two hours of physiotherapy in the first week. Clear documentation of mobilisation in 85% (97/113).
setting: Queen Elizabeth The Queen Mother Hospital, Margate, Kent; main orthopaedic ward and outlier wards
cycle1_result: 93% (106/113) seen by a physiotherapist on the day of or day after surgery (main orthopaedic ward 94%, 80/85; outliers 93%, 21/28; P=0.3). 40% (46/113) had delayed mobilisation. 83% (94/113) had two hours of physiotherapy in the first week. Clear documentation of mobilisation in 85% (97/113).
intervention: not reported
other_findings: Reasons for delayed mobilisation: post-operative delirium 32.6% (15/46), low haemoglobin 26% (12/46), pain 21.7% (10/46), dementia 4.3% (2/46), no documented reason 15.2% (7/46). Presence of one or more of these factors was associated with one-year mortality of 25.8% (16/62, P=0.05), with delirium the strongest single factor (P=0.01).

finding: Overall compliance 76.04% (1244/1636). THR documented as considered in 43.6% (193/443) of eligible patients; 56.43% of THR-indicated patients had no documented consideration (65.41% in 2020).

cycle1_result: ONS provided or prescribed for 182/385 (47.3%) of older adults having hip fracture surgery. ONS was more likely if malnourished on formal testing (OR 11.92; 95% CI 6.57, 21.69).

finding: Median time from ED presentation to MRI 5.9 hours (IQR 4.9–14.7) although median MRI request to scan was 1.7 hours (IQR 1.1–3.7), meeting the GIRFT target; 8% of patients incorrectly sent to the GP-led MEDOCC service. At PDSA 1: 38% of MRIs unnecessary, 0.5 CES MRIs/day, time to analgesia 5.3 hours (IQR 3.8–7.0), 9% inappropriately triaged to MEDOCC.
change: Three PDSA cycles (July 2023 to January 2024): CES working group and trust-level awareness; new locally adapted SOP based on the GIRFT pathway with CES-specific shorter MRI sequences; ED triage and assessment posters, board round, grand round and senior-led teaching. Planned extension of MRI hours was not achieved.
setting: Medway Maritime Hospital, Gillingham; district general hospital emergency department without on-site emergency spinal surgery
cycle1_result: Median time from ED presentation to MRI 5.9 hours (IQR 4.9–14.7) although median MRI request to scan was 1.7 hours (IQR 1.1–3.7), meeting the GIRFT target; 8% of patients incorrectly sent to the GP-led MEDOCC service. At PDSA 1: 38% of MRIs unnecessary, 0.5 CES MRIs/day, time to analgesia 5.3 hours (IQR 3.8–7.0), 9% inappropriately triaged to MEDOCC.
intervention: Three PDSA cycles (July 2023 to January 2024): CES working group and trust-level awareness; new locally adapted SOP based on the GIRFT pathway with CES-specific shorter MRI sequences; ED triage and assessment posters, board round, grand round and senior-led teaching. Planned extension of MRI hours was not achieved.
cycle2_period: PDSA 3, cycles run July 2023 to January 2024
cycle2_result: Approximately 27 patients per cycle. Median ED presentation to MRI 5.7 hours (IQR 4.1–14.3), primary aim not met; GIRFT 4-hour request-to-scan target met in all cycles. cycle1_result: Median time to surgery 39 h (IQR 24–48) on DOACs, 25 h (IQR 20–39) on no antithrombotic and 27 h (IQR 20–44) on other antithrombotics; DOAC patients had higher odds of surgery >36 h (aOR 3.65, 95% CI 2.40–5.55); 43% of DOAC patients had surgery within 36 h versus 61% on other antithrombotics.

finding: 28 (73.7%) had surgery (19 ORIF, 9 revision). Of these, 22 (78.6%) were full weight-bearing, 4 (14.3%) limited weight-bearing and 2 (7.2%) non-weight-bearing. One fixation failure (3.5%).
change: Results presented at a local orthopaedic educational meeting on aiming for immediate full weight-bearing; no re-audit reported.
setting: Dorset County Hospital, district general hospital trauma and orthopaedics; data from the Hip Fracture Registry
cycle1_result: 28 (73.7%) had surgery (19 ORIF, 9 revision). Of these, 22 (78.6%) were full weight-bearing, 4 (14.3%) limited weight-bearing and 2 (7.2%) non-weight-bearing. One fixation failure (3.5%).
intervention: Results presented at a local orthopaedic educational meeting on aiming for immediate full weight-bearing; no re-audit reported.

cycle1_result: Referral compliance 70%, 15% below the provider's internal national average and 25% below its 95% internal target.

finding: Criterion 1 (fibula superimposed by posterior tibia) 83%; criterion 2 (talar domes superimposed) 61%; criterion 3 (open uniform tibiotalar joint) 69%; criterion 4 (landmarks included) 99%.
change: Posters in the emergency department and orthopaedic on-call room/radiography suites, and a teaching session by a foot and ankle associate specialist for orthopaedic staff and radiographers.

cycle1_result: Criterion 1 (fibula superimposed by posterior tibia) 83%; criterion 2 (talar domes superimposed) 61%; criterion 3 (open uniform tibiotalar joint) 69%; criterion 4 (landmarks included) 99%.

topic: Soft tissue knee injury pathway timescales and MRI use
title: A Retrospective Audit of the Timescales Involved in the Diagnosis and Management of Soft Tissue Knee Injuries at a Single National Health Service Trust: A Quality Service Improvement and Redesign Project.
standard: NHS Constitution RTT standard (92% of consultant-led pathways completed within 18 weeks); Diagnostics DM01 standard (<1% waiting over six weeks for MRI); BOA/BOAST and regional MSK guidance of MRI within two weeks where diagnosis uncertain, with review within 7-14 days; NICE CKS and EBI guidance on selective MRI
finding: MRI utilisation 77.7% (269/346). Median waits: presentation to knee clinic 7 days, MRI referral to scan 33 days, scan to review 22 days; median presentation to diagnosis 60 days and to definitive management 97 days. 58.0% waited over four weeks for MRI; only 11.9% scanned within one week; 10.3% reviewed within seven days and 26.2% within 14 days. 42.8% of MRIs normal/degenerative.
setting: Acute knee clinic, Ashford and St Peter's Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (single NHS trust)
cycle1_result: MRI utilisation 77.7% (269/346). Median waits: presentation to knee clinic 7 days, MRI referral to scan 33 days, scan to review 22 days; median presentation to diagnosis 60 days and to definitive management 97 days. 58.0% waited over four weeks for MRI; only 11.9% scanned within one week; 10.3% reviewed within seven days and 26.2% within 14 days. 42.8% of MRIs normal/degenerative.
intervention: not reported
other_findings: Surgery in 11.0% (38/346) with median 128 days from presentation to operation; only 7.2% of non-operative patients started physiotherapy within 30 days of clinic (median 70.5 days). GP referrals had longer median time to diagnosis (74 days) than UTC (53.5) or ED (58); a physiotherapy-first, criteria-based MRI pathway and re-audit were proposed.

finding: Marker ball present in 27 (45%). Of these, entirely visible 16 (59%) and correctly positioned 11 (41%); overall compliance 59% (n=16).

cycle1_result: Marker ball present in 27 (45%). Of these, entirely visible 16 (59%) and correctly positioned 11 (41%); overall compliance 59% (n=16).

topic: ENT casualty management of common acute presentations

finding: Tympanic membrane integrity documented in otitis externa 34.3%; nasal fracture reviewed within 7 days 58.3%, MUA within 14 days 92.9%; SSNHL audiogram within 24 hours 33.3%; epistaxis cautery for visible vessel 87.2%, documentation of counselling 28.0%.

cycle1_period: 5 weeks (10 consecutive weeks over both cycles)
cycle1_result: Tympanic membrane integrity documented in otitis externa 34.3%; nasal fracture reviewed within 7 days 58.3%, MUA within 14 days 92.9%; SSNHL audiogram within 24 hours 33.3%; epistaxis cautery for visible vessel 87.2%, documentation of counselling 28.0%.

topic: Hip fracture analgesia and nerve block

finding: FICB performed 26/40 (65%); contraindications documented in 0/14 (0%) without FICB; pain re-evaluation within 30 min 21 (52.5%); mean time to first analgesia 130 ± 28.8 min; mean time to FICB 228 ± 36.2 min.
change: Practical sessions to familiarise ED clinicians with FICB, and a mandatory analgesia checklist for all suspected neck of femur fractures (pain scores, analgesia times, FICB details and reason if not given).
setting: Emergency department, Macclesfield District General Hospital
cycle1_result: FICB performed 26/40 (65%); contraindications documented in 0/14 (0%) without FICB; pain re-evaluation within 30 min 21 (52.5%); mean time to first analgesia 130 ± 28.8 min; mean time to FICB 228 ± 36.2 min.

cycle1_result: Catheterisation consistent with best practice in 20 (91%); indication clearly documented in 8 (36%); none removed in ED (0%).
intervention: Guideline created on indications for catheterisation; education session for medical and nursing staff planned.
other_findings: Re-audit planned.

title: Improving Delirium Care: A Retrospective Audit of Early Detection and Management Practices
standard: HSE National Guidelines: 4AT cognitive screening within 24 hours, delirium and risk factor documentation, non-pharmacological management and antipsychotic use
finding: Cognitive screening within 24 hours in 34% (n=16); delirium documented in 8.5% (n=4); 15% (n=7) newly prescribed antipsychotics within 24 hours, 57% (n=4) of whom lacked a formal delirium diagnosis.

cycle1_result: Cognitive screening within 24 hours in 34% (n=16); delirium documented in 8.5% (n=4); 15% (n=7) newly prescribed antipsychotics within 24 hours, 57% (n=4) of whom lacked a formal delirium diagnosis.
intervention: not reported
other_findings: Of those screened, 75% (n=12) were abnormal. A 'Delirium Tool' for 4AT and PINCH-ME risk factors with education sessions and re-audit were planned.

title: An Examination of EOL Trajectories and Audit of EOL Documentation In Patients Admitted Under the Department for Older Persons Services
standard: Oxford Audit Assessment Tool for Care of the Dying (1–5 point scale)
finding: Greater than 90% of patients had satisfactory, good or excellent end-of-life documentation.
setting: Department for Older Persons Services, Mercy University Hospital, Cork
cycle1_result: Greater than 90% of patients had satisfactory, good or excellent end-of-life documentation.
intervention: not reported
other_findings: One-third of deaths were acutely unwell, one-fifth followed a dwindling trajectory, 15% had known specialist palliative care needs and about 10% had an unexpected cardiac arrest.

topic: DNACPR and ceilings of care documentation
title: DNAR: All or Nothing: Impact of Education Sessions Re-Audit in a Model 3 Hospital
standard: National HSE guidelines on DNAR and ceilings of care documentation
finding: DNAR status in medical notes 35%; reasoning 32%; patient discussion documented 45%; reasons if excluded 41%; relatives' discussion 48%; reasons if excluded 18%.
change: Two education sessions for NCHDs and consultants.
setting: Adult medical inpatients, Sligo University Hospital (Model 3 hospital)
cycle1_result: DNAR status in medical notes 35%; reasoning 32%; patient discussion documented 45%; reasons if excluded 41%; relatives' discussion 48%; reasons if excluded 18%.
intervention: Two education sessions for NCHDs and consultants.
cycle2_result: DNAR status 35% and reasoning 32% (unchanged); patient discussion 61%; reasons if excluded 66%; relatives' discussion 48%; reasons if excluded 25%.

title: 2833 Quality improvement project on increasing antimicrobial stewardship and patient safety
standard: Microguide local antimicrobial guidance; indication, route, duration and choice of antibiotic
finding: 99 of 168 patients on antibiotics; Microguide compliance 39-65% (mean 53%); indication and duration on drug charts 89%.
change: Weekly microbiology consultant-led ward rounds, education for junior doctors, nurses and consultants, streamlined IT access to Microguide, AMS meetings and prescribing in simulation sessions.
setting: Six geriatric wards, Broomfield Hospital, Mid-South Essex NHS Foundation Trust
cycle1_result: 99 of 168 patients on antibiotics; Microguide compliance 39-65% (mean 53%); indication and duration on drug charts 89%.
intervention: Weekly microbiology consultant-led ward rounds, education for junior doctors, nurses and consultants, streamlined IT access to Microguide, AMS meetings and prescribing in simulation sessions.
cycle2_result: Compliance 70-90% (mean 83%); indication and duration on drug charts 95%.
other_findings: Co-amoxiclav (n = 45) and Tazocin (n = 14) were the most used antibiotics; co-amoxiclav for UTI and Tazocin without microbiology approval were targeted.
authors: Tarkas T; Suthahar Y
citation: Tarkas T, Suthahar Y. 2833 Quality improvement project on increasing antimicrobial stewardship and patient safety. Age and Ageing. 2025;54(Supplement_1). doi:10.1093/ageing/afae277.018.

intervention: Poster highlighting the importance of considering deprescribing in frail patients.

title: 2669 Diagnosing delirium on the Care of the Elderly Ward: a quality improvement project
standard: NICE guidelines: 100% of patients on geriatric wards to have delirium considered via the 4AT
finding: 50.7% (21) suspected delirious; of these 9.5% (2) had a delirium assessment on the same day.
change: Lanyard prompt card with the 4AT distributed to all physicians and a departmental teaching session on delirium for juniors (PDSA).
setting: Care of the Elderly wards, Chelsea and Westminster Hospital
cycle1_result: 50.7% (21) suspected delirious; of these 9.5% (2) had a delirium assessment on the same day.
intervention: Lanyard prompt card with the 4AT distributed to all physicians and a departmental teaching session on delirium for juniors (PDSA).
cycle2_result: 36% (14) suspected delirious; of these 43% (6) had a 4AT score on the same day.

title: 3225 Delirium assessments in an acute frailty ward: an audit of current practice
standard: NICE Delirium Guidelines (CG103)
finding: Initial admission proforma used in 86% of admissions; 53% had completed delirium assessments; delirium prevalence 25%; resuscitation forms 86%; CFS 60%.
change: Admission proforma co-developed with patients and the MDT was modified based on feedback.

cycle1_result: Initial admission proforma used in 86% of admissions; 53% had completed delirium assessments; delirium prevalence 25%; resuscitation forms 86%; CFS 60%.
intervention: Admission proforma co-developed with patients and the MDT was modified based on feedback.
cycle2_result: Modified proforma used in 94%; delirium assessments completed in 79%; delirium diagnosed in 43%; resuscitation forms 93%; CFS 79%.
other_findings: These were cycles three and four of an ongoing project. Delirium and CFS 6/7 were associated with longer length of stay.

title: 3209 Route to a streamline transient ischemic attack pathway: a quality improvement initiative
standard: 2023 National Clinical Guideline for Stroke for the UK and Ireland
finding: Pre-pathway: 10.1% seen directly via AMU; median LoS 1.08 days; 28.2% managed within 24 hours; CT brain 94.8%; stroke specialist review 82.1%; inpatient echo 42.9%.
change: New TIA pathway encouraging an ambulatory approach via the Acute Medical Unit.
setting: Galway University Hospital
cycle1_result: Pre-pathway: 10.1% seen directly via AMU; median LoS 1.08 days; 28.2% managed within 24 hours; CT brain 94.8%; stroke specialist review 82.1%; inpatient echo 42.9%.
intervention: New TIA pathway encouraging an ambulatory approach via the Acute Medical Unit.
cycle2_result: 28.5% seen directly via AMU; median LoS 0.65 days; 35.7% managed within 24 hours; neuroimaging 96.4%; CT 89.3%; MRI without prior CT 75%; stroke specialist review 96.4%; echo 35.7%, Holter 21.4%.
other_findings: Admission under the stroke service rose from 26% to 42.9%, with shorter LoS under AMU or stroke services.

standard: All new stroke admissions to have IPC applied by the post-take consultant ward round unless contraindicated
finding: 21.6% did not have IPC applied on time.
change: Posters in doctors' offices and nursing bases reminding staff to prescribe and apply IPC.
setting: Stroke ward, Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham
cycle1_result: 21.6% did not have IPC applied on time.
intervention: Posters in doctors' offices and nursing bases reminding staff to prescribe and apply IPC.
cycle2_result: 18.1% did not have IPC applied on time (3.5% improvement).
other_findings: Timely prescribing by doctors improved by 5.9% but nursing application worsened by 2.2%.

topic: Dementia and delirium care in hospital
title: Improving Care for Patients with Dementia with Development of a Dementia Friendly Specialist Geriatric Ward: A Quality Improvement Initiative
standard: Irish National Audit of Dementia-2 (INAD-2) recommendations and National Clinical Guideline 21 dementia care standards
finding: Overall compliance 69%; delirium recognition 53%; nutritional care 84%; food within reach 38%; safe mobility 80%; pain assessment 0%; personal preferences documented 40%.

cycle2_result: Overall compliance 87%; delirium recognition 89%; nutritional care 95%; food within reach 100%; safe mobility 100%; pain assessment 100%; personal preferences 88%; antipsychotic prescribing practices improved by 37%.

title: Audit of Traumatic Brain Injury Management at the National Major Trauma Centre
standard: Irish national trauma guidelines for specialist ward admission and neurosurgical referral
finding: 123 (60.6%) managed on trauma wards; 29 (14.3%) needed intensive care; 28 (13.8%) transferred to a neurosurgical centre, with GCS change the only significant predictor (p = 0.017).
setting: National Major Trauma Centre, Mater Misericordiae University Hospital, Dublin
cycle1_result: 123 (60.6%) managed on trauma wards; 29 (14.3%) needed intensive care; 28 (13.8%) transferred to a neurosurgical centre, with GCS change the only significant predictor (p = 0.017).
intervention: not reported
other_findings: 107 (52.7%) were aged ≥65; their 30-day mortality was 7.4% vs 2% and median stay 9 vs 5 days. A TBI unit has opened and a second cycle is planned.
authors: O'Loughlin S; Jonsson A; Gaffney L; Mason C
citation: O'Loughlin S, Jonsson A, Gaffney L, Mason C. Audit of Traumatic Brain Injury Management at the National Major Trauma Centre. Age and Ageing. 2025;54(Supplement_4). doi:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.054.

cycle1_result: Compliance 70% for Question 1, 36.7% for Question 2 and 23.3% for Question 3; 66.7% documented follow-up actions based on responses.

other_findings: not reported

title: A Clinical Audit Of Current Assessment Of Falls In The Older Adult by the Pathfinder Service
standard: 2022 World Guidelines for falls prevention and management; target 100% documentation of eight key assessments
finding: Falls risk stratification 12.5%; other domains not given individually.
change: Eight practice changes aligned with the World Falls Guidelines (delirium screen, lying/standing BP, ECG, standardised balance and gait, ADL and environmental assessments, risk stratification, 3 key questions).
setting: Pathfinder service (National Ambulance Service and University Limerick Hospital Group), patients who fell at home without admission
cycle1_result: Falls risk stratification 12.5%; other domains not given individually.
intervention: Eight practice changes aligned with the World Falls Guidelines (delirium screen, lying/standing BP, ECG, standardised balance and gait, ADL and environmental assessments, risk stratification, 3 key questions).

title: Audit of Stroke Unit Admissions to A University Teaching Hospital (2022–2024)
standard: National Stroke Strategy 2022–2027: 90% of stroke patients admitted to a stroke unit for at least 90% of their hospital stay
finding: Annual admissions 512, 561 and 571; stroke unit admission rates 66%, 69% and 64%; 39%, 36% and 40% stayed on the stroke unit for at least 90% of their stay.

cycle1_result: Annual admissions 512, 561 and 571; stroke unit admission rates 66%, 69% and 64%; 39%, 36% and 40% stayed on the stroke unit for at least 90% of their stay.
intervention: not reported
other_findings: Main barrier to stroke unit admission was lack of bed availability, followed by infection control requirements and clinical decisions such as ICU or palliative care; demand exceeded capacity by a factor of two.

cycle1_result: Mood assessment completed in 71.7% (367/512).

cycle1_result: 9 patients (47.5%) on aspirin for primary prevention.

title: Late Doses, Lost Function: A Hospital Audit of Parkinson’s Medication in Older Adults
standard: NICE guidelines on Parkinson's disease
finding: 30% (9/30) received all PD medications on time; 70% (21/30) had at least one missed or delayed dose; 40% (12/30) had doses omitted; 50% (15/30) delayed (median 2.3 hours); prescribing errors in 20% (6/30).
change: Staff education to support understanding and compliance.
setting: Beaumont Hospital, Dublin (level 4 hospital)
cycle1_result: 30% (9/30) received all PD medications on time; 70% (21/30) had at least one missed or delayed dose; 40% (12/30) had doses omitted; 50% (15/30) delayed (median 2.3 hours); prescribing errors in 20% (6/30).
intervention: Staff education to support understanding and compliance.
other_findings: Reasons for missed or delayed doses were absent in 76% (22/30); formal medication reconciliation in only 13% (4/30); no significant difference between medical and surgical services (p=0.64). Re-audit planned in 6 months.
authors: O'Flanagan G; Quinlan E; Plant R; Khan M
citation: O'Flanagan G, Quinlan E, Plant R, Khan M. Late Doses, Lost Function: A Hospital Audit of Parkinson’s Medication in Older Adults. Age and Ageing. 2025;54(Supplement_4). doi:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.154.

topic: Clinic non-attendance and text message reminders

intervention: not reported

standard: Local algorithm/Trust protocol for doctors (allocated team or on-call) participating in Mental Health Act assessments.

cycle1_result: At least one trust doctor involved in 91% of assessments (92% in Section 136 suite; 89% out of hours).
intervention: not reported
other_findings: 45% detained under section 2 and 35% under section 3; substance misuse part of 26% of assessments. Recommended amending the Section 136 form to record the doctor's role.

topic: Behaviour that challenges in learning disability
title: Retrospective Analysis of a Single Centre Experience of the Pharmacological Management of Patients With Intellectual Disability & Challenging Behaviour Across Three Audit Cycles
standard: NICE and STOMP guidelines for pharmacological management of challenging behaviour in intellectual disability.
finding: Risk assessment 68%; description of target behaviours 74%; metabolic monitoring 0%; documentation of interventions 48%; mental health evaluation 87%; physical health 61%; consent 19%; side-effect discussion 32%; 6-week efficacy review 52%.
setting: Intellectual Disability Team, large acute mental health trust (Leicestershire Partnership NHS Trust)
cycle1_result: Risk assessment 68%; description of target behaviours 74%; metabolic monitoring 0%; documentation of interventions 48%; mental health evaluation 87%; physical health 61%; consent 19%; side-effect discussion 32%; 6-week efficacy review 52%.

other_findings: Middle cycle 2014 (n=17). Polypharmacy declined, with single-drug therapy 19%, 35%, 34%; outpatient-dependent standards worsened, partly due to COVID-19 service pressures.

topic: Early intervention in psychosis waiting times
title: Pathways to Care at Early Intervention in Psychosis Liverpool: A Cross-Sectional Retrospective Audit Cycle
standard: NICE access and waiting time standard: 60% of people with first episode psychosis treated with an approved care package within two weeks of referral
finding: Average referral pathway time 9.8 days
change: Recommendations from the initial audit implemented (details not reported)
setting: Early Intervention in Psychosis team, Liverpool
cycle1_result: Average referral pathway time 9.8 days
intervention: Recommendations from the initial audit implemented (details not reported)
cycle2_result: Average pathway time 22.5 days, exceeding the NICE standard

topic: Physical health assessment on psychiatric admission

standard: Trust protocol for admission blood tests including fasting plasma glucose and HbA1c
finding: 23 (57.5%) had HbA1c or plasma glucose on admission; only 6 (15%) had plasma glucose, not specified as fasted; 17 (42.5%) had neither.

cycle1_result: 23 (57.5%) had HbA1c or plasma glucose on admission; only 6 (15%) had plasma glucose, not specified as fasted; 17 (42.5%) had neither.
intervention: not reported

topic: Physical health assessment on psychiatric admission
title: Audit and Re-Audit: Improving Standardised Admission Blood Tests Adherence for Psychiatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) Patients
standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists Standards for Inpatient Mental Health Services: standardised admission blood tests within 24 hours of admission
finding: 30% had bloods within 24 hours; 40% declined or unsafe; 20% not done in timeframe; 69% of direct admissions had all relevant bloods
change: Standardised PICU guideline with a pre-filled blood test request form
setting: Psychiatric Intensive Care Unit, Kent and Medway NHS and Social Care Partnership Trust
cycle1_result: 30% had bloods within 24 hours; 40% declined or unsafe; 20% not done in timeframe; 69% of direct admissions had all relevant bloods
intervention: Standardised PICU guideline with a pre-filled blood test request form
cycle2_result: Only 6% not done within timeframe; all consenting direct admissions (89%) had all standardised bloods; bloods within 24 hours increased from 80% to 94%; direct admissions with all bloods 77% to 100%

title: The Management of Short-Term Insomnia for Inpatients in an Adult Acute Admissions Ward: Audit of Compliance With Local and National Guidelines
standard: Local and national guidance: sleep hygiene advice before drugs; non-benzodiazepine hypnotic prescribed; one-off trial dose before regular prescription; target 100%
finding: Of 8 reviewed for insomnia: 12.5% (n=1) offered sleep hygiene advice; 25% (n=2) trial dose of non-benzodiazepine hypnotic; 25% (n=3) regular hypnotic with no trial dose; 50% (n=4) alternative sedative.
change: Planned: sleep hygiene leaflet, presentation of data to medical and nursing staff, guidelines made available on the ward; re-audit in six months.
setting: Adult Acute Admissions Ward, West of Scotland
cycle1_result: Of 8 reviewed for insomnia: 12.5% (n=1) offered sleep hygiene advice; 25% (n=2) trial dose of non-benzodiazepine hypnotic; 25% (n=3) regular hypnotic with no trial dose; 50% (n=4) alternative sedative.
intervention: Planned: sleep hygiene leaflet, presentation of data to medical and nursing staff, guidelines made available on the ward; re-audit in six months.
other_findings: The cohort reviewed was 21 patients, of whom 8 were reviewed for insomnia.
authors: Long M; Widdowson R

standard: Mental Health Act 1983 Code of Practice: medical review within 1 hour, 4-hourly until first MDT review, twice daily thereafter with at least one by the Responsible Clinician, with specified documentation content

setting: Psychiatric Intensive Care Unit, Cheshire and Wirral Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
cycle1_result: 20% seen within 1 hour; 75% seen 4-hourly until MDT review; mental health documented 97%, physical health 61%, medication 69%, rationale for continuing 72%, adverse medication effects and observation level 2%, risk to self 7%

change: Local guidelines and letter template with recommended headings, and formal teaching for junior doctors

title: Management of medically assisted withdrawal from alcohol in acute adult mental health and specialist addictions in-patient services: UK clinical audit findings.
standard: not reported
finding: 908 patients on acute adult wards/PICU and 347 on specialist addictions units; addiction specialist oversight in 33 (4%) of acute ward patients

cycle1_result: 908 patients on acute adult wards/PICU and 347 on specialist addictions units; addiction specialist oversight in 33 (4%) of acute ward patients

topic: Ethnic equity in mental health service access
title: An Audit Exploring Ethnic Inequalities in Accessing Perinatal Mental Health Services in Southwark
standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists gold standards for equitable access to perinatal mental health care.
finding: Ethnicity not documented in 6.6% of referrals; no clear inequity at referral, but 3 of 4 admissions (75%) were Black women and all detained; only 2/35 Asian and Mixed ethnicity women referred for psychology; 83% (5/6) of antipsychotics prescribed to Black women; 48% of 31 safeguarding alerts involved Black women.
setting: Perinatal Mental Health Services, Southwark (South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust)
cycle1_result: Ethnicity not documented in 6.6% of referrals; no clear inequity at referral, but 3 of 4 admissions (75%) were Black women and all detained; only 2/35 Asian and Mixed ethnicity women referred for psychology; 83% (5/6) of antipsychotics prescribed to Black women; 48% of 31 safeguarding alerts involved Black women.
intervention: not reported
other_findings: Authors concluded the service was not meeting RCPsych gold standards for equitable care.
authors: Morgan W; Butler J
citation: Morgan W, Butler J. An Audit Exploring Ethnic Inequalities in Accessing Perinatal Mental Health Services in Southwark. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(Suppl 1):S171-S171.

title: Inpatient Ward Review Documentation Audit
standard: 80% completion of ward review documentation questions considered satisfactory
finding: Most questions did not meet the 80% standard; 'Responsible clinician' completed in 23.3%.
change: Strategies to improve record keeping, including automation of some fields, junior doctor induction teaching and awareness posters.
setting: 7 psychiatry wards, Essex Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
cycle1_result: Most questions did not meet the 80% standard; 'Responsible clinician' completed in 23.3%.
intervention: Strategies to improve record keeping, including automation of some fields, junior doctor induction teaching and awareness posters.
cycle2_result: 9 questions satisfactory (at least 80%); 7 above 45%; 17 low; 'Responsible clinician' 99.5% after automation.
other_findings: Effectiveness of non-automated strategies was limited; making fields mandatory or auto-complete worked best.
authors: Nurlu D; Raoof A
citation: Nurlu D, Raoof A. Inpatient Ward Review Documentation Audit. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(S1):S172-S173. doi:10.1192/bjo.2023.454.

title: Physical Health Monitoring in Patients on Antipsychotics: A Clinical Audit
standard: NICE yearly physical health monitoring (BMI, BP, ECG, bloods, alcohol and smoking status); audit standard 100%
finding: BMI recorded 91.67% (n=33); BP 86.11% (n=31); alcohol, smoking and drug use 97.22% (n=35); ECG not recorded in 72.22% (n=26); up-to-date bloods 75% (n=27); QRISK not collected in 22.73% (5/22)
setting: Early Intervention Service first episode psychosis team, Sussex Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
cycle1_result: BMI recorded 91.67% (n=33); BP 86.11% (n=31); alcohol, smoking and drug use 97.22% (n=35); ECG not recorded in 72.22% (n=26); up-to-date bloods 75% (n=27); QRISK not collected in 22.73% (5/22)
intervention: not reported

standard: Trust Antipsychotic Physical Health Monitoring Shared Care Guidelines.

setting: Stroud Recovery community mental health service, Gloucestershire Health and Care NHS Foundation Trust
cycle1_result: 30/37 (81%) with EUPD ever prescribed antipsychotics; 24 (80%) had no licensed comorbid indication; mean duration 36.79 months; 12 (50%) had more than one antipsychotic; only 10 (42%) had prescriptions reviewed to stop or reduce; none offered routine physical review.

topic: Mental health triage form use in the emergency department

standard: RCEM recommendation (in line with NCEPOD 'Treat as One') to use a mental health proforma; local Mental Health Triage Form.

cycle1_result: 98.1% notified adequately with letters to patient and GP; risk assessment completed in 50.9%; risk assessment updated in 25%; contingency plan reviewed for 26 patients; family contacted for 3.

cycle1_result: 49% had information available to out-of-hours GPs

standard: Trust TOE sedation guidelines (midazolam dosing)

cycle1_result: Midazolam doses exceeding Trust guidelines were given, especially risky in under 18 and over 60 year-olds.
intervention: Paediatric sedation dosing section added to Trust guidelines and pre-procedure checklist updated with age and maximum midazolam dose.
other_findings: Changes accepted at clinical governance meeting; re-audit needed.

title: Rapid access rather than open access leads to improved effectiveness of an ENT emergency clinic.
standard: National guidelines on safe clinic numbers
finding: 45% attended without primary care assessment; mean wait 75 minutes; clinic numbers above safe levels; 60% of attendances inappropriate.
change: Open access clinic changed to appointment-based Rapid Access Clinic with trained triage nurse, improved record keeping and formal post-consultation communication.
setting: ENT emergency clinic
cycle1_result: 45% attended without primary care assessment; mean wait 75 minutes; clinic numbers above safe levels; 60% of attendances inappropriate.
intervention: Open access clinic changed to appointment-based Rapid Access Clinic with trained triage nurse, improved record keeping and formal post-consultation communication.
cycle2_result: 43% fewer patients; clinic numbers at safe levels; mean waiting time fell 70% to 22 minutes; inappropriate referrals halved.
other_findings: not reported
authors: Smyth C; Moran M; Diver C; Hampton S
citation: Smyth C, Moran M, Diver C, Hampton S. Rapid access rather than open access leads to improved effectiveness of an ENT emergency clinic. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2013;2(1):u200524.w996. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u200524.w996. PMID: 26734173.

title: Improving treatment provision of Wet AMD with intravitreal ranibizumab.
standard: Royal College of Ophthalmologists' recommendations on appointment intervals for ranibizumab treatment
finding: Appointment system did not meet standards and visual outcomes were poorer than trial standards.
change: Changes to the appointment system, expansion of the treatment facility and employment of additional staff.
setting: Macular treatment centre, Manchester Royal Eye Hospital
cycle1_result: Appointment system did not meet standards and visual outcomes were poorer than trial standards.
intervention: Changes to the appointment system, expansion of the treatment facility and employment of additional staff.
cycle2_result: Appointment standards reached Royal College recommendations; visual outcomes approached landmark study standards.
other_findings: Regular re-audits were used between cycles.
authors: Ghazala F; Hovan M; Mahmood S
citation: Ghazala F, Hovan M, Mahmood S. Improving treatment provision of Wet AMD with intravitreal ranibizumab. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2013;2(1):u201733.w993. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u201733.w993. PMID: 26734182.

title: Successful implementation of strategies to transform Emergency Department transfusion practice.
standard: not reported
finding: 3209 units ordered; 39.5% transfused; 9.5% (289 units) unaccounted for.
change: Staff education, monthly traceability reports, ED transfusion guideline, blood fridge moved to resuscitation room, named transfusion consultant and link nurse, and hospital transfusion group representation.
setting: Emergency department, Scotland (with Scottish National Blood Transfusion Service)
cycle1_result: 3209 units ordered; 39.5% transfused; 9.5% (289 units) unaccounted for.
intervention: Staff education, monthly traceability reports, ED transfusion guideline, blood fridge moved to resuscitation room, named transfusion consultant and link nurse, and hospital transfusion group representation.
cycle2_result: 1034 units ordered (64% reduction); 687 transfused (39% reduction); 68% increase in proportion transfused; 9 units unaccounted for (96% reduction).
other_findings: SNBTS spent £306,437 less in 2011 than 2007 on ED transfusion requests.
authors: Reed MJ; Kelly SL; Beckwith H; Innes CJ; Manson L
citation: Reed MJ, Kelly SL, Beckwith H, Innes CJ, Manson L. Successful implementation of strategies to transform Emergency Department transfusion practice. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2013;2(1):u201055.w690. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u201055.w690. PMID: 26734190.

title: Introduction of 'Anaphylaxis Packs' to improve patient safety in a hospital setting.
standard: Immediate availability of 1:1000 adrenaline for anaphylaxis
finding: Adrenaline unavailable on 50% of audited wards; staff lacked knowledge of anaphylaxis management and drug location.
change: Anaphylaxis packs (adrenaline, chlorphenamine, hydrocortisone, algorithm) added to crash trolleys and checklist, piloted on four wards via PDSA then trust-wide.
setting: Adult wards, hospital
cycle1_result: Adrenaline unavailable on 50% of audited wards; staff lacked knowledge of anaphylaxis management and drug location.
intervention: Anaphylaxis packs (adrenaline, chlorphenamine, hydrocortisone, algorithm) added to crash trolleys and checklist, piloted on four wards via PDSA then trust-wide.
cycle2_result: 100% ward stock of anaphylaxis packs, more consistent drug location and improved staff knowledge.
other_findings: 17 coded anaphylaxis incidents in 2011.
authors: Meade S; Douglas J
citation: Meade S, Douglas J. Introduction of 'Anaphylaxis Packs' to improve patient safety in a hospital setting. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2013;2(1):u464.w346. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u464.w346. PMID: 26734203.

title: Can a multi-factorial assessment and interventional programme decrease inpatient falls in an elderly care ward?
standard: Target 20% reduction in inpatient falls rate
finding: 14.70 falls per 1000 bed days.
change: Falls risk care plan, 'walking-stick' incentive poster for nurses and post-fall guidelines, with staff feedback sessions.
setting: Elderly care ward
cycle1_result: 14.70 falls per 1000 bed days.
intervention: Falls risk care plan, 'walking-stick' incentive poster for nurses and post-fall guidelines, with staff feedback sessions.
cycle2_result: 12.44 falls per 1000 bed days, a 15.4% reduction.
other_findings: Care plan compliance 89%; up to 81% of patients high-risk. 20% target not yet met.
authors: Gibson RS; Heaney A; Hull K
citation: Gibson RS, Heaney A, Hull K. Can a multi-factorial assessment and interventional programme decrease inpatient falls in an elderly care ward?. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2013;2(1):u200500.w332. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u200500.w332. PMID: 26734206.

title: Warfarin Management Pathway: A clear and safe algorithm, from admission to discharge.

cycle1_result: Errors on warfarin charts audited (numbers not stated)
intervention: Warfarin management algorithm emailed to all doctors and laminated copies attached to pneumatic tube system machines
cycle2_result: Marked decrease in chart errors and incomplete anticoagulation referrals (numbers not stated)

authors: Hart-George A

cycle1_result: Suspected DVT often over- and inadequately investigated (numbers not stated)

topic: Extended VTE prophylaxis after abdominal cancer surgery

title: The management of ureteric stones in the Accident and Emergency department.

cycle1_result: No easily accessible, specific criteria were used to guide which patients were admitted and which discharged.

other_findings: not reported
authors: Dawson K; Dawson L

title: Electronic prescribing: Reducing delay to first dose of antibiotics for patients in intensive care.

cycle1_result: Delays in antibiotic administration quantified (numbers not stated)

title: Investigating the bundle compliance of IVIG delivery in the Greater Manchester Neuroscience centre.

cycle1_result: Nine areas delivered to all 75 patients; no patient received the complete bundle
intervention: Electronic treatment dashboard for chronic IVIG therapy

title: Pre-operative fasting - a patient centered approach.
standard: Royal College of Nursing guidelines: minimum fasting of six hours for food and two hours for clear fluids before elective anaesthesia or sedation
finding: Policy stated nothing to eat or drink from midnight/7AM; patients not encouraged to drink clear fluids up to two hours before surgery; 70% subjective dehydration, 40% clinical evidence of dehydration; longest fast 17 hours.
change: Staff teaching session on current fasting guidelines, a corrected patient information leaflet, and reminder posters of the updated policy.
setting: Moorfields South Pre-operative Assessment Unit, St George's Hospital
cycle1_result: Policy stated nothing to eat or drink from midnight/7AM; patients not encouraged to drink clear fluids up to two hours before surgery; 70% subjective dehydration, 40% clinical evidence of dehydration; longest fast 17 hours.
intervention: Staff teaching session on current fasting guidelines, a corrected patient information leaflet, and reminder posters of the updated policy.
cycle2_result: All patients encouraged to drink clear fluids until two hours before surgery; 25% subjective dehydration, 25% clinical evidence of dehydration; longest fast eight hours.
other_findings: Patients in cycle 1 reported the instructions were clear despite being non-compliant with guidance.
authors: Hamid S
citation: Hamid S. Pre-operative fasting - a patient centered approach. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2014;2(2):u605.w1252. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u605.w1252. PMID: 26734235.

title: Tonsillectomy discharge information - An improvement in both patient safety and satisfaction.
standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England standards for tonsillectomy discharge information
finding: 35% had post-operative bleeding information on discharge summary; 51% received no written information; 66% recalled verbal explanation; 54% knew to go to A&E if bleeding; 40% not satisfied (35 telephone questionnaire respondents).
change: Focus group; tonsillectomy patient leaflet produced with bleeding instructions and nearest A&E contact details, revised after patient feedback.
setting: Guy's and St Thomas' Hospital
cycle1_result: 35% had post-operative bleeding information on discharge summary; 51% received no written information; 66% recalled verbal explanation; 54% knew to go to A&E if bleeding; 40% not satisfied (35 telephone questionnaire respondents).

cycle1_result: 37% weighed on admission; 27% had weight on drug chart; 18 (25% of patients on paracetamol) inappropriately dosed

title: Management of anaemia and blood transfusion in critical care - implementing national guidelines in ICU.
standard: British Committee for Standards in Haematology 2012 guidelines: transfuse at haemoglobin below 70 g/L unless bleeding, sepsis, neurological injury or acute coronary syndrome
finding: Before intervention, of 10 transfusions 2 appropriate (green), 1 inappropriate (red) and 7 unclear (amber).
change: Local transfusion guideline with posters in the ICU, then guidance attached to transfusion prescriptions.
setting: Single ICU, North Bristol Trust
cycle1_result: Before intervention, of 10 transfusions 2 appropriate (green), 1 inappropriate (red) and 7 unclear (amber).
intervention: Local transfusion guideline with posters in the ICU, then guidance attached to transfusion prescriptions.
cycle2_result: After both interventions 7 green and 3 amber transfusions, none inappropriate; total ICU transfusions fell by about 50% (41 to 18) after the first intervention.
other_findings: 30 random transfusions analysed in total; began with an audit of doctors' knowledge of transfusion thresholds.

standard: SIGN guideline 117: dexamethasone before tonsillectomy
finding: 73% compliance.
change: ENT secretaries added 'Dex Please' to tonsillectomy theatre lists; after cycle 2, a reminding tool for secretarial staff.
setting: ENT, Royal Devon and Exeter Trust
cycle1_result: 73% compliance.
intervention: ENT secretaries added 'Dex Please' to tonsillectomy theatre lists; after cycle 2, a reminding tool for secretarial staff.
cycle2_result: Third cycle: all lists had 'Dex Please' and compliance was 100%.
other_findings: Second cycle compliance 87% (note implemented in half of cases); readmissions 5, 3 and 2 across cycles, all underdosed; 149 patients in total.
authors: Bola S; Bartlett A; Williams R
citation: Bola S, Bartlett A, Williams R. Perioperative dexamethasone administration in tonsillectomy patients: A three-cycle audit showing improvement using printed theatre lists. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2015;4(1):u208428.w3339. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u208428.w3339. PMID: 26734456.

topic: Old age psychiatry new patient assessment quality

title: Audits show that specialist paediatric training programmes are sensitive to medical, staffing and economic changes.
standard: Modified European Union of Medical Specialists 1997 protocol

change: Follow-up of poorly performing key areas; increase in paediatric specialist resources.

title: Time for a culture change? Suboptimal compliance with blood culture standards at a district hospital in Cape Town.
standard: 2010 South African guideline for blood cultures (22 standards); contamination benchmark 3%
finding: Contamination 4.5%; 33% of bottles had the recommended 8-10 mL fill; 96.9% of patients had a single culture in 24 hours; 7.8% had a combined volume of at least 20 mL; median needle-to-incubator time 11 hours 25 minutes.
setting: A district hospital in Cape Town
cycle1_result: Contamination 4.5%; 33% of bottles had the recommended 8-10 mL fill; 96.9% of patients had a single culture in 24 hours; 7.8% had a combined volume of at least 20 mL; median needle-to-incubator time 11 hours 25 minutes.
intervention: not reported
other_findings: 12.5% of cultures grew organisms; pathogen yield after antibiotic exposure 4.9% vs 7.5% without (p=0.3). A re-audit was recommended.
authors: Abrahams MS; Whitelaw AC; Orth H
journal: South African medical journal = Suid-Afrikaanse tydskrif vir geneeskunde
citation: Abrahams MS, Whitelaw AC, Orth H. Time for a culture change? Suboptimal compliance with blood culture standards at a district hospital in Cape Town. S Afr Med J. 2015;105(12):1039-1043. doi:10.7196/samj.2015.v105i12.9442. PMID: 26792162.

title: Improving the Medical Assessment of Patients Before Electroconvulsive Therapy: An Audit Across Two Sites.
standard: Scottish ECT Accreditation Network standards
finding: Site A: repeat examination in 30 (100%), incomplete in 47%, histories accurate in 20%. Site B: repeat in 6/26 (23%), incomplete in 100%, histories accurate in 38%.
change: Amended examination sheet and prompts to use multiple sources for medical history (site A).
setting: Two ECT sites, NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde
cycle1_result: Site A: repeat examination in 30 (100%), incomplete in 47%, histories accurate in 20%. Site B: repeat in 6/26 (23%), incomplete in 100%, histories accurate in 38%.
intervention: Amended examination sheet and prompts to use multiple sources for medical history (site A).
cycle2_result: Site A: all 12 had complete repeat examination; histories accurate in 8 (67%); multiple sources used in 11 (92%).
other_findings: Oral examination was frequently missed at both sites.
authors: Driver HR
citation: Driver HR. Improving the Medical Assessment of Patients Before Electroconvulsive Therapy: An Audit Across Two Sites. J ECT. 2016;32(2):116-118. doi:10.1097/yct.0000000000000304. PMID: 26807625.

title: Improvement of fluid balance monitoring through education and rationalisation.
standard: Fluid balance monitoring only when clinically indicated, with complete and accurate charts

change: E-learning and verbal presentations on fluid balance, plus daily medical review of charts to rationalise monitoring.
setting: Respiratory ward, Musgrove Park Hospital, large district general hospital
cycle1_result: Only 53% of input/output monitoring was clinically indicated; average chart completion 50%.
intervention: E-learning and verbal presentations on fluid balance, plus daily medical review of charts to rationalise monitoring.
cycle2_result: 93% reduction in unnecessary monitoring, with increases in completion (40%) and accuracy (48%) of remaining charts.
other_findings: not reported
authors: Vincent M; Mahendiran T
citation: Vincent M, Mahendiran T. Improvement of fluid balance monitoring through education and rationalisation. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2015;4(1):u209885.w4087. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u209885.w4087. PMID: 26893885.

topic: Community mental health referral to assessment time

cycle1_result: Compliance low, with only four of 17 standards rated good; physical monitoring especially poor.

topic: Dementia and delirium care in hospital

finding: Hand hygiene compliance poor on induction; no cannula surveillance (VIP scoring) in place.
change: Intensive education, training, demonstrations and coworking; introduction of peripheral cannula care and VIP scoring.
setting: 1000-bed urban hospital in an unnamed partner nation (UK Defence Medical Services Defence Healthcare Engagement)
cycle1_result: Hand hygiene compliance poor on induction; no cannula surveillance (VIP scoring) in place.
intervention: Intensive education, training, demonstrations and coworking; introduction of peripheral cannula care and VIP scoring.

journal: Journal of the Royal Army Medical Corps

topic: High-risk prescribing and monitoring in primary care
